1	---
2	title: Working with scalar lists
3	description: 'How to read, write, and filter by scalar lists / arrays.'
4	url: /orm/v6/prisma-client/special-fields-and-types/working-with-scalar-lists-arrays
5	metaTitle: Working with scalar lists/arrays (Concepts)
6	metaDescription: 'How to read, write, and filter by scalar lists / arrays.'
7	---
8	
9	[Scalar lists](/orm/v6/reference/prisma-schema-reference#-modifier) are represented by the `[]` modifier and are only available if the underlying database supports scalar lists. The following example has one scalar `String` list named `pets`:
10	
11	```prisma highlight=4;normal tab="Relational databases"
12	model User {
13	  id   Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
14	  name String
15	  pets String[] // [!code highlight]
16	}
17	```
18	
19	```prisma highlight=4;normal tab="MongoDB"
20	model User {
21	  id   String   @id @default(auto()) @map("_id") @db.ObjectId
22	  name String
23	  pets String[] // [!code highlight]
24	}
25	```
26	
27	Example field value:
28	
29	```json5
30	["Fido", "Snoopy", "Brian"]
31	```
32	
33	## Setting the value of a scalar list
34	
35	The following example demonstrates how to [`set`](/orm/v6/reference/prisma-client-reference#set-1) the value of a scalar list (`coinflips`) when you create a model:
36	
37	```ts
38	const createdUser = await prisma.user.create({
39	  data: {
40	    email: "eloise@prisma.io",
41	    coinflips: [true, true, true, false, true],
42	  },
43	});
44	```
45	
46	## Unsetting the value of a scalar list
47	
48	:::warning
49	
50	This method is available on MongoDB only in versions
51	[3.11.1](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/3.11.1) and later.
52	
53	:::
54	
55	The following example demonstrates how to [`unset`](/orm/v6/reference/prisma-client-reference#unset) the value of a scalar list (`coinflips`):
56	
57	```ts
58	const createdUser = await prisma.user.create({
59	  data: {
60	    email: "eloise@prisma.io",
61	    coinflips: {
62	      unset: true,
63	    },
64	  },
65	});
66	```
67	
68	Unlike `set: null`, `unset` removes the list entirely.
69	
70	## Adding items to a scalar list
71	
72	:::warning
73	
74	Available for:
75	
76	- PostgreSQL in versions [2.15.0](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/2.15.0) and later
77	- CockroachDB in versions [3.9.0](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/3.9.0) and later
78	- MongoDB in versions [3.11.0](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/3.11.0) and later
79	
80	:::
81	
82	Use the [`push`](/orm/v6/reference/prisma-client-reference#push) method to add a single value to a scalar list:
83	
84	```ts
85	const userUpdate = await prisma.user.update({
86	  where: {
87	    id: 9,
88	  },
89	  data: {
90	    coinflips: {
91	      push: true,
92	    },
93	  },
94	});
95	```
96	
97	In earlier versions, you have to overwrite the entire value. The following example retrieves user, uses `push()` to add three new coin flips, and overwrites the `coinflips` field in an `update`:
98	
99	```ts
100	const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
101	  where: {
102	    email: "eloise@prisma.io",
103	  },
104	});
105	
106	if (user) {
107	  console.log(user.coinflips);
108	
109	  user.coinflips.push(true, true, false);
110	
111	  const updatedUser = await prisma.user.update({
112	    where: {
113	      email: "eloise@prisma.io",
114	    },
115	    data: {
116	      coinflips: user.coinflips,
117	    },
118	  });
119	
120	  console.log(updatedUser.coinflips);
121	}
122	```
123	
124	## Filtering scalar lists
125	
126	:::warning
127	
128	Available for:
129	
130	- PostgreSQL in versions [2.15.0](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/2.15.0) and later
131	- CockroachDB in versions [3.9.0](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/3.9.0) and later
132	- MongoDB in versions [3.11.0](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/3.11.0) and later
133	
134	:::
135	
136	Use [scalar list filters](/orm/v6/reference/prisma-client-reference#scalar-list-filters) to filter for records with scalar lists that match a specific condition. The following example returns all posts where the tags list includes `databases` _and_ `typescript`:
137	
138	```ts
139	const posts = await prisma.post.findMany({
140	  where: {
141	    tags: {
142	      hasEvery: ["databases", "typescript"],
143	    },
144	  },
145	});
146	```
147	
148	### `NULL` values in arrays
149	
150	:::warning
151	
152	This section applies to:
153	
154	- PostgreSQL in versions [2.15.0](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/2.15.0) and later
155	- CockroachDB in versions [3.9.0](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/3.9.0) and later
156	
157	:::
158	
159	When using scalar list filters with a relational database connector, array fields with a `NULL` value are not considered by the following conditions:
160	
161	- `NOT` (array does not contain X)
162	- `isEmpty` (array is empty)
163	
164	This means that records you might expect to see are not returned. Consider the following examples:
165	
166	- The following query returns all posts where the `tags` **do not** include `databases`:
167	
168	  ```ts
169	  const posts = await prisma.post.findMany({
170	    where: {
171	      NOT: {
172	        tags: {
173	          has: "databases",
174	        },
175	      },
176	    },
177	  });
178	  ```
179	
180	  - ✔ Arrays that do not contain `"databases"`, such as `{"typescript", "graphql"}`
181	  - ✔ Empty arrays, such as `[]`
182	
183	  The query does not return:
184	  - ✘ `NULL` arrays, even though they do not contain `"databases"`
185	
186	The following query returns all posts where `tags` is empty:
187	
188	```ts
189	const posts = await prisma.post.findMany({
190	  where: {
191	    tags: {
192	      isEmpty: true,
193	    },
194	  },
195	});
196	```
197	
198	The query returns:
199	
200	- ✔ Empty arrays, such as `[]`
201	
202	The query does not return:
203	
204	- ✘ `NULL` arrays, even though they could be considered empty
205	
206	To work around this issue, you can set the default value of array fields to `[]`.
207

Based on `apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v6/prisma-client/queries/relation-queries.mdx` ("Filter on '-to-one' relations") and `.../special-fields-and-types/working-with-scalar-lists-arrays.mdx` ("Filtering scalar lists"):

Your syntax is actually correct — for a to-one relation like `company`, you can nest scalar-list filters directly (no `is`/`some` needed since `company` is to-one, not a list):

```ts
company: {
  parking: { has: req.body.parkingState }
}
```

This is valid Prisma syntax and combines fine inside your `AND` array. If it's still not filtering as expected, check:

1. **Value match** — `has` requires an exact array-element match (case/format sensitive), unlike `contains` on strings.
2. **Schema in sync** — confirm `parking String[]` was actually migrated and the generated client is up to date.

If you can share the actual (unexpected) result vs. expected, that'd help pinpoint it — but the query shape itself matches the documented pattern.
